title: Learned call analysis identifies receiver-specific marmoset vocal patterns
summary: Classifiers identified receiver-related structure in calls from ten captive marmosets. Playback experiments also found stronger responses to calls originally directed at the listener. The authors interpret these patterns as vocal labels; a later commentary disputes whether the evidence establishes name-like reference, and the authors defend that interpretation. The bounded finding is receiver-specific acoustic and behavioral differentiation, not decoded human-like names.

evidence.tested: Recorded calls and playback responses were analyzed.
evidence.unknown: Name-like reference and alternative explanations remain debated; the captive sample is small.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest acoustic classifiers supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary published-paper Methods and abstract, PubMed metadata, critical commentary abstract and authors response abstract.
